rounds.text: Melstar Information Technologies Ltd is exhibiting a powerful earnings turnaround, evidenced by compounded profit growth of 88% over the trailing twelve months [E7], a staggering net profit increase of 201% year-on-year [E40], and accelerating earnings growth [E43]. This momentum is underpinned by a robust three-year median return on equity of 43% [E11] (alternatively noted at 42.7% [E35]), significantly outperforming typical baselines. Furthermore, capital expenditure has effectively cleared, with Capital Work-In-Progress (CWIP) dropping to Rs 0 Cr, marking a -100% change that signals newly completed capacity ready to generate returns [E22]. Demonstrating immense internal conviction, promoter shareholding has surged dramatically by 47.51 percentage points to reach 94.57% as of September 2026 [E23]. Finally, the stock trades at an accessible 1.19 times its book value [E1], presenting an attractive entry point relative to its accelerating operational performance. Conceded: [E4] and [E19].

Melstar Information Technologies Ltd carries severe fundamental vulnerabilities that undermine its valuation and operational stability. The company's profitability and capital efficiency are deeply compromised, evidenced by a negative ROCE of -18.1% and a sharp ROE decline to -36.0% [E4, E5]. Long-term top-line erosion is pronounced, with compounded sales growth at -31% over 10 years, accompanied by a 10-year compounded share price growth of -1% [E6, E8]. Furthermore, the balance sheet exhibits high leverage risk as the debt-to-equity ratio stands at 2.29x with borrowings expanding to Rs 11.68 Cr in September 2026, while operations burn cash with a negative operating cash flow of Rs -2.19 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -2.44 Cr [E17, E18, E19, E21]. Working capital management is heavily strained by extraordinarily high debtors of 701 days, and the business faces compounding pressures from low interest coverage alongside potential interest cost capitalization [E36, E37, E38]. Conceded: the company shows short-term earnings momentum with an 88% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a 3-year median ROE of 43% [E7, E11], alongside a massive promoter holding increase to 94.57% [E23].

The bear highlights a negative ROCE of -18.1% and a ROE drop to -36.0% [E4, E5], but this ignores the robust 3-year median ROE of 43% which reflects solid mid-term capital returns [E11]. Conceded: 10-year sales growth is -31% and 10-year share price growth is -1% [E6, E8], yet earnings momentum has aggressively reversed with trailing twelve-month profit growth hitting 88% alongside a 201% year-on-year net profit surge [E7, E40]. While debt stands at Rs 11.68 Cr with a 2.29x debt-to-equity ratio [E19, E21], capital expenditure has completely cleared out as capital work-in-progress fell 100.0% to Rs 0 Cr, signaling that major capacity projects are now online [E22]. Conceded: operating cash flow is negative at Rs -2.19 Cr and free cash flow sits at Rs -2.44 Cr [E17, E18], but insiders are heavily backing this operational inflection with promoters aggressively raising their stake by 47.51 percentage points to a massive 94.57% [E23]. Finally, dismissing the current valuation overlooks the fact that results score 81 out of 100 for accelerating turnaround metrics, proving that stale sentiment is masking active operational progress [E43, E46].

Conceded: 3-year median ROE stands at 43% [E11], but this historical comfort is completely overridden by the current severe reality where ROE has collapsed to -36.0% and ROCE sits at an alarming -18.1% [E4, E5]. While the bull points to trailing profit growth of 88% and a 201% year-on-year profit surge [E7, E40], this coexists with an inconsistent operating margin trend [E14, E15] and a deeply negative TTM operating margin of -14% [E13]. The claim that zero CWIP signals completed capacity coming online [E22] ignores the severe balance sheet stress where borrowings have swollen to Rs 11.68 Cr [E21], driving the debt-to-equity ratio to an unsustainable 2.29x [E19] alongside flagged risks of low interest coverage and potential interest capitalization [E36, E37]. Conceded: promoters aggressively raised their stake to 94.57% [E23], but heavy insider ownership cannot negate the immediate cash burn of negative operating cash flow at Rs -2.19 Cr and negative free cash flow at Rs -2.44 Cr [E17, E18]. Finally, leaning on an accelerating turnaround score [E43, E46] dismisses the profound fundamental warning of crippling 701-day debtors [E38] and a disastrous historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -99.8% [E29].
